title: Nothing can be created in the cluster (an admission webhook deadlock)
intro: After a node failure overnight, every 'kubectl apply' and every new pod in the cluster is rejected with an 'Internal error ... failed calling webhook'. Existing pods keep running. A policy engine was installed last month as a validating admission webhook, in the namespace policy-system.

steps.prompt: Reproduce it: try to create a pod named test from the nginx image in the default namespace.
steps.fake_output: Error from server (InternalError): Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "validate.policy.example.com": failed to call webhook: Post "https://policy-webhook.policy-system.svc:443/validate?timeout=10s": no endpoints available for service "policy-webhook"

steps.prompt: The API server can't reach the webhook's Service. List the validating webhook configurations.
Look at how policy-check is configured.
steps.fake_output:
webhooks:
- name: validate.policy.example.com
  clientConfig:
    service: {name: policy-webhook, namespace: policy-system, path: /validate}
  failurePolicy: Fail
  rules:
  - operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    apiGroups: ["*"]
    resources: ["*"]
  namespaceSelector: {}
  timeoutSeconds: 10
steps.hint: Look at failurePolicy, the rules, and namespaceSelector.

steps.prompt: It applies to every resource in every namespace and fails closed. Check the webhook's own pods in policy-system.
steps.fake_output: No resources found in policy-system namespace.

steps.prompt: Its pods died with the node, and replacements can't be created, because creating a pod requires the webhook. Break the deadlock: patch policy-check so the webhook's failurePolicy is Ignore.
Now the webhook's pods can be scheduled again. Wait for its deployment policy-webhook in policy-system to roll out.
steps.fake_output:
Waiting for deployment "policy-webhook" rollout to finish: 0 of 2 updated replicas are available...
deployment "policy-webhook" successfully rolled out

resolution: A validating admission webhook is called by the API server before objects are stored. With failurePolicy: Fail, an unreachable webhook means every matching request is rejected. This one matched every resource in every namespace, including its own, so when its pods were lost, the replacement pods needed the webhook's approval to exist: a deadlock that takes out the whole cluster's ability to change anything. Setting failurePolicy to Ignore temporarily let the pods be created; set it back to Fail once the webhook is healthy, if the policy is security-critical. The durable fixes are in the webhook's configuration: exclude its own namespace and kube-system with a namespaceSelector, run several replicas spread across nodes with a PodDisruptionBudget, and keep the timeout short. The same reasoning applies to mutating webhooks (service meshes, secret injectors). When 'nothing can be created' and the error mentions a webhook, look at the webhook configurations first.
